hypothesis_2026_09_08: The seller's 'pm3' mark correlates with presenting a GENUINE-looking identity. The four pm3-marked tags (three SLIX at IC ref 0x01, SLIX-S at 0x02) all carry NXP's manufacturer byte with an IC reference matching the part they claim, and proxmark identifies every one. The five unmarked tags all present something off: IC ref 0x21 on a SLIX that should read 0x01, IC ref 0x8B with an unregistered manufacturer byte 0x53 on the silver pair, an unregistered 0x48 on the gold, and IC ref 0x22 on the keychain. A plausible reading is that the unmarked ones are emulators carrying a programmed CFG -- which is what produces an odd IC ref -- while the pm3 ones are genuine NXP silicon made magic some other way. THIS IS A HYPOTHESIS, not a finding: it is a correlation across nine tags, and the write probe will test it. Note it cuts against the naive expectation, since it predicts the tags proxmark CAN write are the ones that look least like magic.
note: Expectations seeded from seller listings before any tag was read. Measurements are added by tools/iso15693_magic_probe.py; the expected block is never overwritten. Second order recorded 2026-09-08: 9 physical tags across 7 label types, seller-described as a mystery pack. The bag labels use `UID 0-NNB`, which decodes consistently across BOTH orders: `UID` is a claim that the UID is changeable, and `0-NN` is the writable block range, so 0-27B = 28 blocks, 0-63B = 64, 0-55B = 56. Cross-checked against measurement: our 28-block SLI tags, our 64-block TI cards, and the tool's own LRi2K-56 impersonation target all agree. The FIRST order's plain tags were labelled '1024 bit' with NO UID claim and measured non-magic, so the notation distinguishes magic from plain rather than being decoration.

ANOMALY: blocks 0 and 1 would not read -- 6 retries each in baseline and 6 more in capacity, so 12 consecutive failures -- while blocks 2-27 read fine. Capacity aborted entirely, since it needs block 0 as its anchor, so this tag has NO physical measurement. Marginal coupling is the obvious explanation (it is the only tag too large to sit flat on the HF pad) but it does not fit well: coupling drops reads at RANDOM, and this failed the same two addresses every time while its three siblings read all 28 blocks. Re-run it: if 0 and 1 fail again with the tag repositioned, that is a property of the tag rather than the placement.

DESTRUCTIVE-PROBE WARNING: this tag has real memory at blocks 56/57/62/63, so a gen1 attempt OVERWRITES four blocks of it. The out-of-range safety that makes the 28-block tags harmless does NOT apply here. Take a baseline first and check --identify before writing. BLOCK COUNT UNKNOWN AND UNCLAIMED -- the label states no range, and nothing here can supply one: neither proxmark nor this app hardcodes SLIX2 geometry, both read GET SYSTEM INFO, and proxmark's SLIX2-specific GET NXP SYSTEM INFO path carries no size table either. So capacity has to measure it. A guess that it is a large part was recorded here on 2026-09-08 and withdrawn the same day as unsourced -- on the labels alone the largest claimed geometry in this batch is the TI pair at 0-63B, not this tag. Which way it lands decides whether a gen1 attempt is destructive, so measure before writing. || MEASURED 2026-09-08: THE INTERESTING ONE. Advertises 79 blocks x 4 -- so the withdrawn guess that it was the largest tag in the batch was numerically right, and withdrawing it was still correct: there was no source for it and now there is a measurement. uid[1]=0x48, not NXP's 0x04, and 'no tag-info available'. AND IT ANSWERS READS PAST ITS ADVERTISED COUNT: every block from 0 to 81 returned data. The capacity figure of 82 is the probe's own search ceiling (advertised + 2, then +1), NOT the card -- real capacity is >= 82 and unmeasured. Re-run with --capacity-max 255. This is the answers-reads-everywhere archetype that ISO15693_POLLER_PASS_MAX_MS exists for, on an off-the-shelf tag rather than a deliberately programmed one. gen1 IS destructive here.

expected.listing_text: Chip type: I-CODE2, Memory capacity: 1024 bit
expected.note: THE LISTING'S BIT FIGURE IS TOTAL SILICON, NOT USER MEMORY. 1024 bits = 128 bytes = 32 blocks, but an ICODE SLI/SLIX addresses 28 of them as user blocks (28 x 4 = 112 bytes = 896 bits); the remaining 4 blocks are the system/config area. So expect 28, not 32. Reporting 32 would mean the listing quoted USER memory and this is a different part. IC ref 0x01 is the SLI/SLIX family. Expected non-magic.

white-tag-1.note: The probed representative of the three. Classified non-magic on hardware 2026-08-24; the gen1 attempt sent ordinary WRITE BLOCKs at 56/57/62/63, all out of range on a 28-block tag, and block 27 still read its factory 57 5F 4F 4B afterwards -- so no aliasing, and the tag is byte-identical to its baseline.
